newsitem.title: JORDAN: Britain says no softening towards Baghdad.
newsitem.headline: Britain says no softening towards Baghdad.

text.p: Britain's new government said on Wednesday it remained committed to enforcing tough United Nations sanctions on Iraq and would not soften its stance towards Baghdad.

"We hold exactly the same position that the previous administration in the United Kingdom (held)," Foreign Office Minister Derek Fatchett told a news conference in Amman. "The policy objective is to ensure the regime in Iraq meets the criteria in the U.N. Security Council resolutions."
Two weeks ago Iraq welcomed a statement of concern by the new British government when thousands of Turkish troops swarmed into northern Iraq to crush Kurdish rebels.
It said it hoped the two countries could look at their relationship in a new light, "away from the grudges and complexes of the past".
But Fatchett, on a tour of the Middle East, said there was no change of policy in London.
"There will be no softening of the position under the new administration," he said.

Britain, which contributed troops to the U.S.-led military coalition that recaptured the Gulf emirate of Kuwait in 1991 from Iraqi forces, has consistently backed a tough line against Iraqi President Saddam Hussein.
But Iraq says enthusiasm for stringent U.N. trade sanctions, imposed for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait, is waning in other countries.
